entity.name: Hyo Jang
entity.description: I am Hyo Jang (@hyochan), the sole core maintainer working full-time on OpenIAP and its cross-platform in-app purchase libraries. OpenIAP carries forward the react-native-iap community, whose original repository dates to 2017. Active development is in the hyodotdev/openiap monorepo; the original react-native-iap repository is archived as project history. Public sponsorship channels include GitHub Sponsors and OpenCollective. This request supports ongoing maintenance and paid contributor work to share the workload, improve compatibility, and help the existing ecosystem grow sustainably. Hyo Jang is the applicant responsible for this funding plan.

projects.name: OpenIAP including react-native-iap
projects.description: OpenIAP provides open protocols, native implementations, and framework libraries for in-app purchases. Its Client Protocol standardizes purchase APIs and types; its Commerce Protocol standardizes server verification, entitlements, and subscription lifecycle events. The monorepo maintains react-native-iap, expo-iap, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, .NET MAUI, and Godot integrations, alongside Apple and Android packages. In September 2026, npm recorded 589,205 downloads of react-native-iap and 1,036,826 downloads of expo-iap. Download events are not unique users or applications. The legacy react-native-iap repository had 3,223 stars when checked on 12 October 2026; these are historical ecosystem evidence, not OpenIAP monorepo stars. OpenIAP already documents SBOM publication, npm provenance verification, dependency monitoring, and security response. Funding will sustain this existing ecosystem through compatibility updates, issue triage, regression tests, release verification, documentation, and contributor onboarding. Source: https://github.com/hyodotdev/openiap ; download counts: https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/2026-09-01:2026-09-30/react-native-iap and https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/2026-09-01:2026-09-30/expo-iap .

plans.name: One year of OpenIAP maintenance and reliability
plans.description: $100,000 for 12 months: $50,000 for full-time core maintenance; $35,000 for paid contributor tasks on existing SDKs, regression/conformance tests and tooling; $10,000 for CI, test infrastructure and devices; $5,000 for documentation and onboarding. Publish scoped tasks and acceptance criteria in the first quarter, recruit contributors, and report quarterly on work and spending. These are planned allocations; track other grants separately to avoid charging the same work twice.
